# Agentic Foundry

> Ticket-first delivery for agent-built software, shipped as a Claude Code plugin.
> The loop: a ticket with a runnable "Done means" → build in an isolated worktree → local-green
> before push → one PR → the platform's own enforcement (branch protection + CI, honestly tiered)
> → human sign-off. Gates make problems visible, not impossible; the operator's judgment is
> terminal by design.

Key facts for agents: the core loop is three verbs (init, dispatch, merge-when-green); the unit of
work is a GitHub issue whose `## Done means` fenced command is what the session runs before it
stops; the paper guard refuses writes to specs/, docs/, .foundry/ and similar unless the active
ticket allows them; a spec with a frozen, operator-signed acceptance contract is an opt-in lane
(`security: true` work); merge-when-green runs only on explicit instruction; there is no
unattended-merge mode.
